q: Who designed the Lotus Temple in Delhi?
n: The Lotus Temple in Delhi (1986), a Bahá'í House of Worship, was designed by Iranian-born architect Fariborz Sahba. Source: Bahá'í House of Worship, New Delhi, official site.

q: Who designed the Dancing House in Prague, with Vlado Milunić?
n: The Dancing House in Prague (1996), nicknamed Fred and Ginger, was designed by Frank Gehry with Vlado Milunić. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Frank Gehry.

q: Who designed the Gherkin?
n: 30 St Mary Axe (the Gherkin) in London (2004) was designed by Norman Foster (Foster + Partners). Source: Foster + Partners project page.

q: Who designed One World Trade Center?
n: One World Trade Center (2014) was designed by David Childs of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill. Source: SOM project page.

q: Who designed the cathedral inserted into the Mosque–Cathedral of Córdoba?
n: The cathedral nave inserted into the Mosque–Cathedral of Córdoba was begun in 1523 by Hernán Ruiz I. Source: UNESCO (Historic Centre of Cordoba); Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Who designed Dulles International Airport?
n: Washington Dulles International Airport's terminal (1962) was designed by Eero Saarinen. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Eero Saarinen.

q: Who designed Haus Scheu in Vienna?
n: Haus Scheu in Vienna (1912), an early terraced flat-roofed house, was designed by Adolf Loos. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Adolf Loos.

q: Who designed the Centre Pompidou-Metz?
n: The Centre Pompidou-Metz (2010) was designed by Shigeru Ban with Jean de Gastines. Source: Shigeru Ban Architects project page; Pritzker Prize (2014 laureate).

q: Who designed the Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris?
n: The Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris (2014), with its glass "sails", was designed by Frank Gehry. Source: Fondation Louis Vuitton official site.

q: Who designed the Wainwright Building?
n: The Wainwright Building in St. Louis (1891) was designed by Louis Sullivan with Dankmar Adler, an early skyscraper. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Louis Sullivan.

q: Who converted a power station into the Tate Modern?
n: Herzog & de Meuron converted the Bankside Power Station into the Tate Modern, which opened in 2000. Source: Tate official site; Pritzker Prize (2001 laureates).

q: Who designed Finlandia Hall?
n: Finlandia Hall in Helsinki (1971) was designed by Alvar Aalto. Its white marble cladding and fan-shaped concert hall are typical of Aalto's late humane modernism. Source: Alvar Aalto Foundation.

q: Who designed the Villa Savoye?
n: The Villa Savoye at Poissy (1931) was designed by Le Corbusier and embodies his Five Points of Architecture. Source: UNESCO (The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier).

q: Who designed the Walt Disney Concert Hall?
n: The Walt Disney Concert Hall in Los Angeles (2003) was designed by Frank Gehry. Source: LA Phil official site.

q: Which building was the world's tallest from 1913 to 1930, at 792 ft (241 m)?
n: The Woolworth Building in New York, by Cass Gilbert, was the world's tallest building (792 ft, 241 m) from 1913 to 1930. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Woolworth Building.

q: Who was the original architect of the US Capitol?
n: William Thornton won the 1793 design competition and is regarded as the original architect of the US Capitol. Source: Architect of the Capitol (aoc.gov).

q: Who designed the White House?
n: The White House was designed by Irish-born architect James Hoban (1792). Source: White House Historical Association.

q: Who is the architect of the Sears Tower?
n: The Sears (Willis) Tower (1973) was designed by Bruce Graham of SOM, with engineer Fazlur Khan's bundled-tube structure. Source: SOM project page; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Who is the architect of the National Parliament Building in Papua New Guinea?
n: Papua New Guinea's National Parliament House (1984) was designed by architect Cecil Hogan King. Source: National Parliament of Papua New Guinea history.

q: Who designed the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building (Tokyo City Hall)?
n: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building (1991) was designed by Kenzo Tange. Source: Tokyo Metropolitan Government official site; Pritzker Prize (1987 laureate).

q: Who designed the Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium?
n: The Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium (1990) was designed by Fumihiko Maki. Source: Maki and Associates; Pritzker Prize (1993 laureate).

q: Who is the architect of the Grange Road House located in Singapore?
n: Paul Rudolph designed residential towers in Singapore, including the Grange Road project. Source: Paul Rudolph Heritage Foundation.

q: Who is the architect of the Peak Tower in Hong Kong?
n: The present Peak Tower in Hong Kong (1997) was designed by Terry Farrell. Source: Farrells project page.

q: Which Italian architect designed the Padre Pio Pilgrimage Church?
n: The Padre Pio Pilgrimage Church at San Giovanni Rotondo (2004) was designed by Renzo Piano. Source: Renzo Piano Building Workshop project page.

q: Who designed the Getty Center?
n: The Getty Center in Los Angeles (1997) was designed by Richard Meier. Source: Getty official site; Richard Meier & Partners.

q: Which is a famous work of Frank Gehry?
n: The Walt Disney Concert Hall is Frank Gehry's. The Chiat Building (with Oldenburg) is also Gehry's, but Sydney Opera House is Utzon's and the Heydar Aliyev Center is Hadid's. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Frank Gehry.

q: Which Finnish architect worked in Art Nouveau (National Romanticism) early in his career?
n: Eliel Saarinen worked in Finnish National Romanticism (Art Nouveau) early in his career, for example Helsinki Central Station. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Eliel Saarinen.

q: Which Finnish architect also designed glassware, furniture and textiles?
n: Alvar Aalto also designed glassware (the Savoy vase), furniture (the Paimio chair) and textiles. Source: Alvar Aalto Foundation; Artek.

q: Which 21st-century British architect is known for curves, sharp angles and dynamic façades?
n: Zaha Hadid, British-Iraqi and the 2004 Pritzker laureate, is known for sweeping curves, sharp angles and dynamic facades. Source: Pritzker Architecture Prize; Zaha Hadid Architects.

q: Which London glasshouse by Decimus Burton and Richard Turner combines wrought and cast iron?
n: The Palm House at Kew Gardens (1844–48) by Decimus Burton and Richard Turner is a landmark of wrought and cast iron with glass. Source: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew; UNESCO (Kew).

q: Who is called the father of skyscrapers and of modernism?
n: Louis Sullivan of the Chicago School is called the father of skyscrapers and of modernism ("form follows function"). Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Louis Sullivan.

q: Who is the architect of the Opus Place?
n: Richard Meier designed the master plan of Opus Place in Midtown Atlanta. Source: Richard Meier & Partners / developer announcements.

q: Which Japanese architect designed the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park and museum?
n: Kenzo Tange designed the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park and Museum (1955). Source: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum; Pritzker Prize.

q: Which architect designed over 500 projects in the US, most of them houses?
n: Frank Lloyd Wright designed over 1,000 works, of which about 500 were built, most of them houses. Source: Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation.

q: What is the largest aquarium in the Southwest United States?
n: OdySea Aquarium in Scottsdale, Arizona, is billed as the largest aquarium in the Southwest United States. Source: OdySea Aquarium official site.

q: What is the most visited art museum in the world?
n: The Louvre in Paris is the world's most visited art museum, with millions of visitors a year. Source: The Art Newspaper annual visitor figures; Louvre official site.

q: Who belonged to both the New York Five and the Memphis Group?
n: Michael Graves was one of the New York Five and later designed for Ettore Sottsass's Memphis Group, turning to postmodernism. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Michael Graves.
